activation.note: Activation retains the WMBT ownership condition, existential acceptance-bound test threshold, configured topology roots, and scan exclusions. It does not turn the beneath-feature fix hint into a placement requirement. Path facts are directly observable; semantic findings and diff interpretation honestly require new observers.

audit.summary: All 21 segments survive at their claimed destinations, with source metadata and package-guard details retained separately from the coder obligation. The rewrite preserves the single coverage obligation, rationale, recommended fix, and original scan exception; no undeclared additions, waiver creep, or application-specific overfitting were found.

segmentChecks.note: The given/then pair retains the existential rule: every feature owning at least one WMBT needs at least one test bound to one of that feature's acceptances.
The audit field retains the package-guard realization and distinguishes it from a canonical planner node.
The complete per-rule package checks, including the failing fixture and relationship edges, survive verbatim in audit.
All four topology keys, their configuration file, and all four defaults are retained in verifier_detail and used consistently by activation.
The silent-gap rationale is verbatim in why and accurately operationalized in avoid without changing the obligation.
The recommended fix is verbatim in prefer; verifier_detail correctly prevents its beneath-feature wording from becoming a placement requirement.
All four excluded tree names and the never-scanned rule survive in unless, verifier_detail, and activation.
The validator type and atdd_topology reference remain explicit in audit, with the validator report appropriately reused as evidence.

risks: The coder-facing fields do not show the concrete syntax or procedure for binding a test to an acceptance, so an agent unfamiliar with the repository's test annotations could add a test beneath the feature without establishing the required binding.
The phrase 'beneath the feature' does not define the physical directory layout, although prefer makes this a recommendation rather than a second coverage condition.

unobservable: finding=feature-with-wmbts-has-no-bound-test requires a new observer to derive feature/WMBT ownership and acceptance-to-test bindings from plans and scanned tests.
The diff-level change values for adding features/WMBTs and removing or unbinding acceptance-bound tests require a new semantic diff observer.
A topology-root change's effect on whether any scanned acceptance-bound test remains requires semantic binding analysis beyond directly observable file paths.

review.summary: The rewrite preserves the core existential coverage obligation, topology settings, exclusions, package-guard details, and recommended fix without turning test placement into an extra requirement. I agree with the auditor's PASS; applicability is deterministic once the declared semantic observers are available, with only a minor coder-facing gap around concrete binding syntax.
